children: Revenue rises 124 per cent to Rs 340.8 crore in the September quarter, while first-half profit increases 206 per cent year-on-year
GP Petroleums reported a 179 per cent year-on-year increase in profit after tax (PAT) to Rs 15.3 crore in the second quarter of FY27, supported by higher revenue and improved operating performance.

Revenue from operations rose 124 per cent to Rs 340.8 crore in the July-September quarter, compared with Rs 152.4 crore in the corresponding period last year, according to the company’s financial results.

Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) increased to Rs 21.04 crore from Rs 8.2 crore a year earlier, a rise of 157 per cent. The EBITDA margin improved to 6.2 per cent from 5.4 per cent in the year-ago quarter.
GP Petroleums manufactures and markets industrial and automotive lubricants, process oils, greases and specialty products under its IPOL brand.
For the first half of FY27, revenue from operations increased 84 per cent to Rs 571.1 crore from Rs 310.6 crore in the corresponding period of FY26.
EBITDA rose 178 per cent to Rs 49.4 crore, compared with Rs 17.8 crore a year earlier. Profit after tax more than tripled to Rs 36.5 crore from Rs 11.9 crore, marking a 206 per cent increase.
The company said the lubricant sector experienced steady industrial demand during the September quarter, alongside changing raw material conditions and competitive pressures.
Company Plans To Strengthen Working Capital

The company’s board has approved raising up to Rs 130 crore through structured non-convertible debentures (NCDs) and optionally convertible debentures (OCDs) with RevX Special Credit Opportunities Fund II.

According to the company, the proposed fundraising is intended to strengthen working capital and support expansion into specialty products. The company also aims to improve cash flows and increase its market presence.
